content.text:
No — Fly is running Node, not Bun. Nothing in the deploy path touches Bun today:

- `Dockerfile:4-5` — `ARG NODE_VERSION=24` / `FROM node:${NODE_VERSION}-slim`, used for both the build stage and the final image
- deps install with `npm ci` from `package-lock.json`
- `CMD [ "node", "./.output/server/index.mjs" ]` — Nitro's default `node-server` output
- `package.json` declares `"engines": { "node": ">=22.12.0" }` and `"packageManager": "npm@11.12.1"`

The only Bun trace is the untracked `bun.lock` in your working tree (you have Bun 1.4.0 locally), and it isn't committed or used by the image — the Dockerfile only copies `package-lock.json` + `package.json` before installing.

So this isn't a version bump, it's a runtime switch. How far do you want it to go?

questions.question: How much of the Fly build should move to Bun 1.4?

options.label: Runtime only (Recommended)
options.description: Keep the build stage on node:24 + npm ci + vp build, but make the final image oven/bun:1.4-slim and run the Nitro output with `bun ./.output/server/index.mjs`. Smallest blast radius — Vite+/npm toolchain untouched, lockfile stays package-lock.json.
options.preview:
FROM node:24-slim AS build
  ... curl vite.plus, npm ci, vp build, npm prune

FROM oven/bun:1.4-slim
ENV NODE_ENV=production
COPY --from=build /app /app
EXPOSE 3000
CMD ["bun", "./.output/server/index.mjs"]

options.label: Full Bun: install + build + run
options.description: Bun everywhere — `bun install --frozen-lockfile` from a committed bun.lock, `vp build` under Bun, and Bun as the runtime. Means committing bun.lock and dropping package-lock.json; more risk since Vite+ manages package management itself.
options.preview:
FROM oven/bun:1.4-slim AS build
  curl vite.plus
  COPY bun.lock package.json ./
  RUN bun install --frozen-lockfile
  RUN vp build

FROM oven/bun:1.4-slim
CMD ["bun", "./.output/server/index.mjs"]

options.label: Don't change it
options.description: Leave the deploy on Node 24. You were just checking what it runs.

# syntax = docker/dockerfile:1

# Node is used only to build; the runtime image is Bun (see BUN_VERSION below)
ARG NODE_VERSION=24
ARG BUN_VERSION=1.4

# Throw-away build stage to reduce size of final image
FROM node:${NODE_VERSION}-slim AS build

WORKDIR /app

# Install Vite+ CLI (curl needed for installer)
RUN apt-get update -qq && \
    apt-get install -y --no-install-recommends curl ca-certificates && \
    rm -rf /var/lib/apt/lists/* && \
    curl -fsSL https://vite.plus | bash
ENV PATH="/root/.vite-plus/bin:$PATH"

# Install dependencies
COPY --link package-lock.json package.json ./
RUN sed -i 's/"prepare": "vp config"/"prepare": "true"/' package.json && \
    npm ci

# Copy application code
COPY --link . .

# Build application (emits .output/ via Nitro)
RUN vp build

# Drop dev dependencies for the final image
RUN npm prune --omit=dev


# Final stage for app image
FROM oven/bun:${BUN_VERSION}-slim

LABEL fly_launch_runtime="TanStack Start"

# App lives here
WORKDIR /app

# Set production environment
ENV NODE_ENV="production"

# Copy built application
COPY --from=build /app /app

# Start the Nitro node-server output under Bun

content.text:
To answer your question directly: **no, it wasn't using Bun at all** — Fly was running `node:24-slim` with `npm ci` and `CMD ["node", "./.output/server/index.mjs"]`. So this was a runtime switch, not a version bump.

**What I changed** (`Dockerfile`, runtime-only per your pick):
- Build stage stays `node:24-slim` + `npm ci` + `vp build` — Vite+ toolchain untouched
- Final stage is now `oven/bun:1.4-slim` (resolves to Bun 1.4.0), `CMD ["bun", "./.output/server/index.mjs"]`
- Split the old shared `base` stage since the two stages no longer share an image; added `ARG BUN_VERSION=1.4`

**Verified:**
- Nitro output under Bun vs Node, same build: `/blog/$slug` byte-identical, `/` and `/blog` differ only by a timestamp and `Math.random()` particle coords
- `docker build` succeeds; container running Bun 1.4.0 serves `/`, `/blog`, `/blog/$slug`, `/tool`, `/reading-list` all 200, output matching the Node baseline (only asset hashes differ, separate build)
- `vp install`, `vp check`, `vp test run` all pass (17 tests, 4 files)

**One thing I fixed that you should know about:** the first Docker build failed on `npm ci`, and it wasn't Bun's fault — your `package.json` version bumps were never reflected in `package-lock.json` (you have an untracked `bun.lock`, so `bun install` was run instead of `npm install`). **Your Fly deploy was already broken before this change.** Since you chose to stay on npm for installs, I regenerated the lockfile with `npm install --package-lock-only`. It shrank a lot (−1691/+522), but that's deduped nested Babel copies — I confirmed all 324 linux and 113 darwin platform-binary entries survived intact.

**Not verified:** the `askAI` POST server function. It needs `GROQ_API_KEY`, which I don't have locally, and I couldn't pin down its `/_serverFn/` endpoint id after a few tries so I stopped rather than dig further. Low risk — it uses `generateText`, not streaming, so there's no SSE plumbing to diverge — but it's genuinely untested under Bun, and `ai.functions.ts` is one of your uncommitted files.

**I have not deployed.** Two reasons worth your call:
1. `fly deploy --remote-only` uploads the working directory, so it would also ship your uncommitted `src/server/ai.functions.ts` and `src/server/blog.functions.ts` edits.
2. flyctl isn't authenticated here — `fly secrets list` returns "no access token available". You'd need `! fly auth login` first.

Minor, flagging so it's a choice not an oversight: `package.json` still has `"engines": { "node": ">=22.12.0" }` and `"start": "node ./.output/server/index.mjs"`, so local `npm start` and production now use different runtimes. Happy to align those, commit the Dockerfile + lockfile, or run the deploy once you're logged in — just say which.

Run the Fly.io image on Bun 1.4

The deploy image ran Node 24 for both build and runtime. Keep Node +
npm ci + vp build for the build stage so the Vite+ toolchain and
package-lock.json are untouched, and switch only the final stage to
oven/bun:1.4-slim, starting the Nitro node-server output under Bun.

The old shared `base` stage is split since the two stages no longer
share an image.

Verified: the Nitro output serves identically under Bun and Node from
the same build (/blog/$slug byte-identical; / and /blog differ only by
a timestamp and Math.random() particle coordinates), and a container
built from this Dockerfile reports bun 1.4.0 and returns 200 for /,
/blog, /blog/$slug, /tool and /reading-list.

Not exercised: the askAI POST server function, which needs GROQ_API_KEY.
It uses generateText rather than streaming, so there is no SSE plumbing
to diverge.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 5 <noreply@anthropic.com>
Claude-Session: https://claude.ai/code/REDACTED
EOF
)" 2>&1 | tail -3 && git status --short
input.description: Create branch and commit Dockerfile only
